cases.fullName: support matrix says exactly what each provider can do and why not
support matrix never claims support without naming a method, and never refuses without a reason
adoption claim requires an explicit acknowledgement and an exact object, and defaults to the safe lifecycle
adoption claim binds the approval digest to the object, the lifecycle, the fields and the resource it is for
adoption claim takes field owners from the registry and refuses a claim that contradicts it
drift baseline captures only known, IaC-owned attributes and records what another owner holds
drift baseline reports drift from the baseline on owned fields and treats another owner's movement as expected variance
drift baseline refuses a baseline too large to record
the claimed object must be the live object accepts only a present, real observation of exactly that object
decommission gate leaves objects Zenith created to the existing guards
decommission gate refuses everything the claim did not allow, with a reason per object
decommission gate allows an adopted object only while its destroy-allowing claim is active and exact, and says which claim
capability inputs are strict references, normalized, and shown to the approver
where the worker may connect classifies addresses
where the worker may connect refuses metadata, loopback and private hosts by default, and a name that resolves to one
owned PostgreSQL 16 TLS DNS transport exports and imports actual databases with fresh independent readback and original-host TLS
owned PostgreSQL 16 TLS DNS transport refuses rebinding after public preflight before any connection to the actual engine
owned PostgreSQL 16 TLS DNS transport revalidates after the actual engine closes an owned session
owned MinIO TLS DNS transport exports actual MinIO bytes and imports them with a fresh independent production-adapter readback
owned MinIO TLS DNS transport refuses rebinding after public preflight without connecting to actual MinIO
owned MinIO TLS DNS transport revalidates a retry after a real MinIO TLS connection closes
validated DNS transport classifies equivalent forbidden literal ::ffff:7f00:1
validated DNS transport classifies equivalent forbidden literal 0:0:0:0:0:ffff:a00:1
validated DNS transport classifies equivalent forbidden literal ::ffff:a9fe:a9fe
validated DNS transport classifies equivalent forbidden literal 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1
validated DNS transport classifies equivalent forbidden literal 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0
validated DNS transport returns validated literals and refuses all answers if one is forbidden without exposing resolver values
validated DNS transport Postgres refuses a private connect answer after a public preflight, without opening a socket
validated DNS transport Postgres connects to the opt-in validated IP while verifying the original hostname and SNI
validated DNS transport Postgres reconnect revalidates changed DNS before creating a replacement socket
validated DNS transport Postgres rejects a trusted certificate for a different hostname
validated DNS transport Postgres never downgrades TLS when the server refuses negotiation
validated DNS transport Postgres literal-IP TLS verifies IP SAN (matching: true)
validated DNS transport Postgres literal-IP TLS verifies IP SAN (matching: false)
validated DNS transport S3 literal-IP TLS verifies IP SAN (matching: true)
validated DNS transport S3 literal-IP TLS verifies IP SAN (matching: false)
validated DNS transport S3 refuses a private connect answer after its public preflight with no request or value leakage
validated DNS transport S3 TLS uses the validated IP and preserves signed Host and original-host certificate identity
validated DNS transport S3 rejects a trusted certificate for a different hostname
validated DNS transport S3 retry revalidates changed DNS and never opens a second socket to a forbidden answer
validated DNS transport S3 does not follow an HTTP redirect to another authority
validated DNS transport private opt-in never allows metadata, including hexadecimal mapped IPv6
object store export copies every object byte for byte, with its content type, and verifies the artifact from storage
object store export exports an empty bucket as a valid, restorable empty export
object store export refuses a bucket over the object or size limits instead of exporting part of it
object store restore, verified by readback from the target restores into an empty bucket and a separate listing-and-hashing pass reads the same content back
object store restore, verified by readback from the target reports a mismatch when an object changes between restore and readback
object store restore, verified by readback from the target never merges into a non-empty bucket, and refuses a changed artifact before writing anything
object store restore, verified by readback from the target computes the same digest regardless of listing order, and a different one when a byte changes
S3 adapter validates the credentials secret and never echoes a value
S3 adapter scopes artifact keys under its base prefix and refuses traversal
S3 adapter speaks the S3 API through the SDK commands (contract: a scripted client, not a service)
LocalStack / S3-compatible endpoint through the production adapter exports one bucket and restores into another, verified by listing and hashing the target
postgres logical export writes a manifest last, lists every file with its digest, and verifies the artifact by reading it back from storage
postgres logical export is idempotent for the same operation and refuses to reuse a location for another
postgres logical export refuses a database holding objects it cannot carry, naming them, and writes nothing
postgres logical export refuses unsupported provider and kind combinations before touching anything
postgres restore into a new target, verified by independent readback restores the artifact alone into an empty database and a re-opened engine reads back the same logical content
postgres restore into a new target, verified by independent readback reports a mismatch, not success, when the target reads back differently
postgres restore into a new target, verified by independent readback never merges into a populated target
postgres restore into a new target, verified by independent readback refuses an artifact that was changed after Zenith recorded it, and one that no longer matches its own manifest
postgres restore into a new target, verified by independent readback refuses to run DDL the exporter would not have written
postgres restore into a new target, verified by independent readback refuses to restore across kinds and into an older major version
independent readback computes the same logical digest from any session, whatever order rows were inserted in
independent readback enforces the export limits instead of exporting a truncated database
real network Postgres through the production connector restores encoded JSON row batches through the production connector and independently reads their exact values
real network Postgres through the production connector exports and restores between two scratch databases of the same server
portability store [pglite] records a verified export once per operation, and refuses a different digest for the same operation
portability store [pglite] derives a restore's verdict from the two digests and only accepts an export of this workspace
portability store [pglite] adopts a referenced resource only under a human approval of the exact operation, atomically with the ownership change
portability store [pglite] refuses to adopt without a human approval, with a stale or foreign approval, for a managed resource, or a second claim on the same object
portability store [pglite] releases an adopted resource back under approval, once, without ever touching the object
